about: Burial places verified one by one against the named source for every entry; figures whose burial place could not be verified were left out.

entries.name: Shaykh al-Tusi
entries.place: Mosque of Shaykh al-Tusi, beside the Imam Ali Shrine
entries.detail: Founder of the Najaf seminary tradition (d. 460/1067). Per his will he was buried in his own house beside the shrine, which became his mosque.

entries.name: Sayyid Muhammad Mahdi Bahr al-Ulum
entries.place: Beside the tomb of Shaykh al-Tusi, Najaf
entries.detail: The great scholar known as Bahr al-Ulum, 'Ocean of Knowledge' (d. 1212/1797), buried next to Shaykh al-Tusi, as are some of his descendants.

entries.name: Shaykh Abbas Qummi
entries.place: Najaf, beside his teacher Mirza Husayn Nuri
entries.detail: Author of Mafatih al-Jinan, the book of duas carried by almost every pilgrim (d. 1359/1941).

entries.name: Al-Allama al-Hilli
entries.detail: The towering jurist of Hilla (d. 726/1325); he is buried in the shrine of Imam Ali (a.s.) in Najaf.

entries.name: Muqaddas Ardabili
entries.detail: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ardabili (d. 993/1585), famous for his piety and his commentary on the Qur'an.

entries.name: Shaykh Murtada al-Ansari
entries.detail: The 'Seal of the Jurists' (d. 1281/1864), author of al-Makasib and al-Rasa'il, teacher of a generation of scholars.

entries.name: Akhund Muhammad Kazim Khurasani
entries.detail: Author of Kifayat al-Usul (d. 1329/1911), the standard advanced text of usul al-fiqh.

entries.name: Mirza Muhammad Husayn Na'ini
entries.place: A room of the courtyard of the Imam Ali Shrine
entries.detail: The great usul scholar (d. 1355/1936), buried in one of the rooms surrounding the courtyard of the holy shrine.

entries.name: Sayyid Abu al-Hasan al-Isfahani
entries.place: A room of the courtyard of the Imam Ali Shrine
entries.detail: Marja' of his age (d. 1365/1946); after a vast funeral he was buried in a room of the shrine courtyard.

entries.name: Sayyid Abu al-Qasim al-Khoei
entries.detail: Grand Ayatollah al-Khoei (d. 1413/1992), teacher of many of today's maraji', buried in the Shrine of Imam Ali in Najaf.

entries.name: Sayyid Muhsin al-Hakim
entries.detail: Grand Ayatollah al-Hakim (d. 1390/1970), founder of schools and libraries across Iraq.

entries.name: Sayyid Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr
entries.detail: Philosopher and martyr (executed 1400/1980), author of Falsafatuna and Iqtisaduna.

entries.name: Prophets Hud and Salih (a.s.)
entries.name_ur: حضرت ہود و صالح علیہما السلام
entries.detail: According to hadith related in the sources, the tombs of the prophets Hud (a.s.) and Salih (a.s.) are situated in Wadi-us-Salam, where a shrine is attributed to them.

entries.name: Kumayl ibn Ziyad
entries.detail: The trusted companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), to whom the Imam taught the famous Dua Kumayl.

entries.name: Habib ibn Muzahir
entries.place: Imam Husayn Shrine — the martyrs' collective grave
entries.detail: The elderly companion who rode out to join Imam Husayn (a.s.); he rests in the collective grave of the martyrs of Karbala inside the shrine.

entries.name: The Martyrs of Karbala (companions of Imam Husayn a.s.)
entries.place: The collective grave (Ganj-e Shohada), Imam Husayn Shrine
entries.detail: The companions and family members who fell on Ashura are buried together in the collective grave within the Imam Husayn Shrine.

entries.name: Shaykh Yusuf al-Bahrani
entries.detail: Author of al-Hada'iq al-Nadira (d. 1186/1772), one of the great fiqh works of the Akhbari tradition.

entries.name: Al-Wahid al-Behbahani
entries.detail: Muhammad Baqir al-Behbahani (d. 1205/1791), reviver of the Usuli school, buried in the Holy Shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.).

entries.name: Mirza Muhammad Taqi al-Shirazi
entries.place: Southern chamber of the Imam Husayn Shrine
entries.detail: Leader of the 1920 revolt against the British occupation (d. 1338/1920), buried in the shrine's southern chamber.

entries.name: Hurr ibn Yazid al-Riyahi
entries.detail: The commander who left Yazid's army on the morning of Ashura and was martyred beside Imam Husayn (a.s.).

entries.name: Aun ibn Abdullah
entries.place: His shrine on the Baghdad–Karbala road
entries.detail: A descendant of Ja'far al-Tayyar; pilgrims stop at his shrine on the road to Karbala.

entries.name: Muslim ibn Aqil
entries.detail: The envoy of Imam Husayn (a.s.) to Kufa, martyred on 9 Dhu al-Hijja 60 AH; his shrine adjoins the Great Mosque.

entries.name: Hani ibn Urwa
entries.place: His shrine beside Dar al-Imara, Kufa
entries.detail: The Kufan elder who sheltered Muslim ibn Aqil and was martyred with him; buried near the Dar al-Imara (governor's palace).

entries.name: Al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
entries.place: Beside the Great Mosque of Kufa
entries.detail: Who rose to avenge the martyrs of Karbala (d. 67/687); buried beside the Mosque of Kufa.

entries.name: Maytham al-Tammar
entries.detail: The date-seller and loyal companion of Imam Ali (a.s.), executed in Kufa shortly before Karbala.

entries.name: Al-Shaykh al-Mufid
entries.detail: Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, 'the Teacher' (d. 413/1022), buried in the holy shrine of Kazimayn near his teacher Ibn Qulawayh.

entries.name: Ibn Qulawayh al-Qummi
entries.place: Inside the Kadhimayn Shrine, beside al-Shaykh al-Mufid
entries.detail: Author of Kamil al-Ziyarat (d. 368/978) — the classical book on the ziyarat of the Imams.

entries.name: Al-Sharif al-Murtada
entries.detail: 'Alam al-Huda (d. 436/1044), elder brother of al-Sharif al-Radi, compiler of Nahj al-Balagha.

entries.name: Khwaja Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
entries.detail: The polymath of Maragha observatory fame (d. 672/1274), buried in the shrine of Kazimayn as he had wished.

entries.name: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni
entries.detail: Compiler of al-Kafi (d. 329/941), the first of the Four Books of hadith; he died in Baghdad and was buried at Bab Kufa.

entries.name: Salman al-Farsi
entries.place: His shrine at Salman Pak, Mada'in
entries.detail: The beloved companion of the Prophet (s), governor of Mada'in, resting at Salman Pak south of Baghdad.

entries.name: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman
entries.place: His shrine at Salman Pak, Mada'in
entries.detail: Companion of the Prophet (s) and keeper of his secrets, visited together with Salman al-Farsi at Mada'in.

entries.name: Narjis Khatun
entries.detail: Mother of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.); her tomb is believed to be located in the al-Askari shrine.

entries.name: Hakima Khatun
entries.detail: Daughter of Imam al-Jawad (a.s.) and aunt of Imam al-Askari (a.s.), narrator of the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (a.t.f.s.).

entries.name: Awn and Muhammad — sons of Lady Zaynab (s.a.)
entries.name_ur: عون و محمد — فرزندانِ بی بی زینب سلام اللہ علیہا
entries.place: With the martyrs of Karbala, at the foot of Imam al-Husayn's (a.s.) grave inside his shrine
entries.detail: The two sons of Lady Zaynab (s.a.) and Abdullah ibn Ja'far were martyred at Karbala on Ashura. They have no separate shrine: like almost all the martyrs of Karbala (apart from Hazrat Abbas, Hurr and Habib, who have their own shrines), they rest in the martyrs' burial place beside Imam al-Husayn's grave — so they are honoured at his shrine, which is already pinned on the map, rather than at a separate pin.
entries.source_name: Guides to the Imam Husayn Shrine / WikiHussain — martyrs of Karbala

entries.name: Sayyid Muhammad ibn Imam Ali al-Hadi (a.s.)
entries.name_ur: سید محمد بن امام علی الہادی علیہ السلام
entries.place: His shrine in Balad, on the Kadhimiya–Samarra road
entries.detail: The eldest son of Imam Ali al-Hadi (a.s.), known as Sab' al-Dujayl ('the Lion of Dujayl'). His shrine is famous for vows (nadhr): devotees bring sheep — the small livestock of the mannat tradition — which are slaughtered at the shrine's own slaughter-place and the food shared with pilgrims, a custom described in his biography. Shown here without a map pin on purpose: published sources disagree about the shrine's exact coordinates by several kilometres, and this app does not pin what it cannot verify.
entries.source_name: Al-Kafeel shrine network / biography of Sayyid Muhammad
